name: Niger
summary: Orange, white and green horizontal bands with an orange disc in the centre, in an unusual nearly square ratio. It was adopted in 1959, before independence from France in 1960.
origin: The Territorial Assembly adopted the flag on 23 November 1959. Niger became independent on 3 August 1960 and kept it; the 6:7 proportions are unusual among national flags.

colors.name: Orange
colors.meaning: The Sahara desert in the north.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Purity and innocence; also the Niger River.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Hope, and the fertile lands of the south and west.

symbols.name: Orange disc
symbols.description: A circle in the centre of the white band.
symbols.meaning: The sun; also read as the sacrifices of the people.

facts: India's flag has the same colour scheme with a blue wheel; Niger's has an orange disc.
Its 6:7 ratio is closer to square than almost any other national flag except Switzerland's and Vatican City's.
Ivory Coast's flag uses the same colours vertically.
clues: Orange, white and green horizontal bands with an orange disc, nearly square.
Its orange stands for a vast desert.
Often confused with a large Asian country's flag that has a wheel.
